items.reason: Repeats the claim that unsupported EC parameter construction and ECDSA key-factory lookup break EC JWK parsing through AbstractJWKParser.
Describes readSequence accepting a child that crosses the declared sequence boundary and returning successfully with a negative remainder.
Describes the same missing sequence-boundary validation, allowing child encodings to exceed the remaining declared content length.
Describes the same acceptance of child encodings extending beyond the sequence's declared length; the different example does not change the problem.
Identifies the same self-consistency-only round-trip assertion, which can pass despite corrupted signature values because no independent correctness check is performed.
Identifies the same default P-256 key generation in every algorithm case, leaving real P-384/P-521 signatures and their encoding sizes untested.
Describes the same readSequence boundary bug: an oversized child makes the remaining length negative without causing rejection.
